parsed.attack: The embed target cannot embed: BIA-accredited nonprofits and community legal clinics are structurally barred from handing a client a paid credit-pack tool that role-plays an officer, because steering a client's interview preparation edges into advising on the case, and their clients are means-tested so the price fails too. The founder's own kill line - 'fewer than 20 ESL classes or clinics pass it on after 3 months of direct outreach' - concedes this is a hand-sold motion where clinic 21 costs the same founder-hours as clinic 1 and nothing compounds. And the user can never refer: the day the interview passes the need is permanently extinguished, and a new citizen does not subsequently meet green card holders with a booked interview date in any context where the app comes up.
parsed.strongest_defence: The audience self-clusters online with no gatekeeper at all - country-specific Facebook groups, r/USCIS and immigration TikTok are enormous, free and turn over in days rather than the 6-12 months community-led growth normally needs - and 'the AI officer asked about a trip I forgot to list' is a share-shaped story that a nervous applicant installs on immediately because their own date is three weeks away.
parsed.verdict_reason: Clinic embedding is linear founder-sold outreach into compliance-averse gatekeepers with a terminal user need, though a fast free online community channel exists under a different loop.
